The derivative of a matrix potential is the induced endomorphism derivative delta_d V=X_d(V)+i[A_d,V], not X_d(V) alone. Write K=-sum k_d nabla_d^2. Two integrations by parts, taking real parts, give 2Re<Ku,Vu>=2sum k_d int(nabla_d u)*V(nabla_d u)-int u*(sum k_d delta_d^2 V)u. No commutation of distinct Haar generators or V with the connection is needed. Therefore ||sum k_d delta_d^2 V||<=C_N(1+|q|^4). Since the minimum matrix eigenvalue of V is >=c_N(1+|q|^4), scalar Young gives, in matrix forms, sum k_d delta_d^2 V <=delta V^2+C_(N,delta)I. Conversely membership in D(K) intersect D(V) supplies an L2 form representative, hence membership in the Friedrichs operator domain. Positivity and upper bounds make D(V)=D(|q|^4). Ktheta and unweighted K have equivalent H2 graph norms: coefficients are bounded smooth and independent of unbounded q, compact-factor elliptic estimates combine with Phi Fourier estimates and bounded affine first-order interpolation.
